material.name: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite
material.composition: NbMoCrTiAl HEA with in-situ formed particles

intervention.description: Design of a novel metal matrix composite by in-situ formation

structure.description: primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina

evidence_units.mechanism: presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al2O3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles
evidence_spans: A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method.
The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail.
The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina.

With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA.

material.name: Nb-Mo-Cr-Ti-Al HEA composite
material.initial_state: elemental powders (Nb, Mo, Cr, Ti, Al; purity >99.5 wt.%; particle size ≤45 μm) mixed in equiatomic composition

intervention.action: high energy planetary ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering
intervention.description: Powders milled in pure argon atmosphere with stearic acid as process control agent and additive, then consolidated via SPS

evidence_units.mechanism: Stearic acid acts as a process control agent to prevent cold welding and particle agglomeration and serves as an additive for generating particulate reinforced HEA composite

outcome.measurement_method: Vickers microhardness tester (MicroMet-5104, Buehler, Lake Bluff, IL, USA)

evidence_spans: The empirical addition amount of stearic acid was 3.5 wt. %.

The stearic acid was introduced as process control agent (PCA) to prevent cold welding as well as particle agglomeration, and also acted as additive for generating particulate reinforced HEA composite.
Subsequently, the as-milled powders were consolidated by SPS (D25/3, FCT, Munich, Germany) under 30 MPa axial pressure at 1700 °C with the heating rate of 100 K/min.
During the sintering process, the sample was held at the sintering temperature for 30 min.
Finally the sample cooled to room temperature in furnace.
Microhardness of the sample was measured by a Vickers microhardness tester (MicroMet-5104, Buehler, Lake Bluff, IL, USA) with an indenter load of 100 g and the holding time was 15 s.

intervention.description: Cylindrical specimens cut and machined from sintered bulk and tested

parameters.specimen_geometry: 4 mm in diameter and 6 mm in height

structure.description: microstructure evaluated by FESEM and XRD

evidence_spans: Cylindrical specimens of compression tests (4 mm in diameter and 6 mm in height) were cut and machined from the sintered bulk.
Room temperature compression tests were carried out on an Instron-3369 (INSTRON, Norwood, MA, USA) universal testing machines at strain rate of 10 −3 s −1 .

material.composition: Nb20.3 Mo31.0 Cr19.3 Ti10.7 Al16.7 (BCC phase) + TiC + Al2O3

microstructure: TiC and Al2O3 evenly distributed at grain boundaries
No debonding between dispersed particles and HEA matrix
defects: Interstitial C and O atoms causing substantial strain fields

evidence_units.mechanism: Second phase strengthening by hard ceramic reinforcements (TiC, Al2O3) and interphase boundary integrity; grain refinement strengthening due to PM process and hard phases acting as barriers to grain growth; solution strengthening by interstitial O and C atoms and substitutional Nb in TiC lattice causing lattice distortion and dislocation interaction

conditions.temperature: not specified (high temperature synthesis and testing implied)

comparison.baseline_state: BCC solid solution without ceramic reinforcements or interstitials

evidence_spans: The composite created a kind of material with highly improved compressive strength, increasing from 1010 MPa to 1542 MPa.

The addition of stearic acid can be used as an effective way for the preparation of composite materials. During the process of high energy ball-milling, PCA is used to not only prevent cold-welding, but also act as the source of the elements carbon and oxygen.

The third reason is the influence of solution strengthening. It is true that the solution element could have remarkable strengthening effect. In this study, the BCC phase contains 0.69 at. % O and 1.28 at. % C, which may cause significant increase in strength because these two interstitial atoms have a substantially smaller size than any of the metal atoms in the HEA.
These interstitial atoms will produce a substantial strain field, with which gliding dislocations will interact.
Therefore, we may reasonably conclude that solution-strengthening effect resulted in the improved mechanical properties.

Another main factor is grain refinement strengthening mechanism. The grain size of the as-homogenized NbMoCrTiAl phase is about 100 μm, while that of the composite is much lower. This is because the PM process is an effective approach to refine grains compared to arc-melting [ [16] ]. In addition, the hard phases evenly distributed at the grain boundary, acting as the barrier of grain growth.

intervention.description: Reaction sintering process to densify the composite

structure.description: Three identifiable phases: light (BCC HEA), grey (TiC), and black (Al2O3)
microstructure: No apparent debonding between dispersed particles and HEA matrix

candidate.mechanism: Good bonding between secondary phase grains and HEA matrix due to reaction sintering
evidence_spans: Microstructure of the NbMoCrTiAl composite after spark plasma sintering at 1700 °C for 30 min under a pressure of 30 MPa.
The specimens are highly densified by the reaction sintering process without visible pores.
The composite presented three obviously identifiable contrasts, namely light, grey, and black regions (marked as A, B, and C).
The volume fraction of the light phase, grey phase, and black phase are 60.8%, 32.2%, and 7.0%, respectively.
The light, grey, and black phase were identified as BCC HEA phase, TiC phase, and Al 2 O 3 phase, respectively.
The average particle size of TiC and Al 2 O 3 were measured to be approximately 4.60 μm and 1.57 μm, respectively.
No apparent debonding between dispersed particles and the HEA matrix could be found, which suggested that the secondary phase grains and the HEA grains possessed good bonding.
Despite no ductility, the fracture strength of the composite was 1542 MPa, increasing by more than a half than that of the as-cast alloy (1010 MPa).
